items.question: How must this teaching be guarded in the world of mortals?
premises: The teaching must be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The mortal world contains the lowest of men
items.inference: This teaching should be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching rightly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient should be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
A chapter is being identified
It is the fifth chapter
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter in the text emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the work that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What understanding has been gained through the grace of the lord of Kaulas?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Understanding arose by his grace
The determination of Kaula is now known
items.inference: By the lord of Kaulas' grace, the speaker has come to know the determination of Kaula.
items.plain_english: O lord of Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul has been declared
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The verse asks who the declared soul is and what its true nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is questioned
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The verse asks where the soul dissolves and requests a full account of it.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The soul is described as the supreme, partless, eternal, and stainless reality.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified as haṃsa and the individual of power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That supreme soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also called the individual of power
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual associated with power.
uncertainties: The exact sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is doctrinally nuanced.
items.plain_english: That soul which is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual of power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
It is described as situated
Its location is in all beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
This departure is described as mere leaving
At that moment it is given a supreme designation
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is called the supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and heard according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes through an unbroken lineage
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as something transmitted through traditional succession.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What effect does merely hearing this knowledge have for the fair-faced one?
premises: The knowledge is merely heard
Hearing itself is emphasized
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even the mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The verse states the cause but leaves the result to be completed by the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice should continue for six months
The practitioner is described as one who undertakes it
The state aimed at is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state symbolized as free from bondage.
uncertainties: The role of kāṣāyaṃ may be literal or symbolic.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months, taking up the ochre robe free from bondage...

items.question: What benefits result from sustained practice of this soul discipline?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with them is achieved
items.inference: Sustained practice leads to freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: He becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: A teaching has been told
The teaching concerns the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to a person endowed with all states and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The phrase sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is open to doctrinal interpretation.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence must not be given
It is the essence of the Kaula teaching
It originates from the yoginīs
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given indiscriminately.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given out.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after receiving this knowledge?
premises: The speaker refers to the present moment
The body is described as pure
It was previously struck by the veil of ignorance
items.inference: The speaker claims that her body is now pure, having been freed from the veil of ignorance.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, no longer struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish
The wish is to hear a teaching
The teaching concerns the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through this teaching?
premises: The speaker promises to explain
There is said to be no doubt
Death will be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching is asserted to destroy death without doubt.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be affected at the tip of nectar by burning essence?
premises: The tip of nectar is involved
There is burning by the essence of juice
Even a wise person is affected
items.inference: Even a wise person may experience burning at the tip of nectar by its potent essence.
uncertainties: The physiological and yogic referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may be burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath at the tongue and palate should be practiced?
premises: The practice is located at the root of tongue and palate
The breath is to be drawn in
It should be done slowly
items.inference: One should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing the breath at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink it in.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are affected
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this technique destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What protection against poison is claimed for one established in this practice?
premises: Poison does not enter the body
This holds even if bitten
The bite may come from great serpents
items.inference: One established in this practice is protected from poison even when bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
